thread:
lea (AE): Quick sync — FinServX wants a 4‑week POC (’sprint zero’) to validate fraud-detection assistant. They gave token estimates but also asked for GPU sizing + cost and the security questionnaire is in flight. Can we align success criteria and sizing?

mike (solutions): Got it. Key Qs: 1) avg vs p95 tokens per request? 2) expected concurrent sessions at peak? 3) do they need streaming? 4) are eval prompts offline or live A/B?

chao (customer): Hi all — thanks. Avg payload ~1.2k tokens, p95 ~6.5k (big context for some cases). Expected peak concurrency ~40 active sessions (short bursts), steady 8 concurrent. Streaming not required for sprint zero. Evaluations: we’ll run set of 1500 labeled prompts offline, plus 50 live sessions.

lea (AE): Timeline: kickoff next Mon, 4 weeks total: week1 infra + ingest, week2 model tuning + evals, week3 integration + load test, week4 final validation + docs. Success criteria draft: - >=92% precision on labeled eval set, - end-to-end 95th percentile latency < 350ms for single-dialog hops, - cost <= $X/day (TBD).

mike (solutions): For the token profile: assume avg 1.2k and p95 6.5k, request rate: steady 8 qps (concurrency) and bursts up to 40 qps for ~2–3 min windows. With that pattern, recommended baseline: 1 x A100‑80GB (pooled) for functional testing + autoscale policy to add a second node during bursts. If they want a firm SLA for p95 latency during bursts, consider 2x A100s pinned.

sanjay (infra): Quick calc I ran locally: with our runtime and a mixed-quant model (~8-bit), tokens/sec per A100 for generation at 1k context ~= 180–220 tokens/s for a single request stream. For p95 6.5k tokens, worst-case generation time ~30–40s single-threaded — but we can parallelize across micro-batches and KV caching for reused prefixes. Realistic estimate for 40 concurrent short requests requires ~1.8–2.5 A100s equivalent.

mike (solutions): TL;DR: For POC (not production): 1x A100 for baseline tests + scheduled scale to 2x for load tests. For production sizing guidance: target 3x for buffer.

ella (security): Security note — they asked about tenant isolation and key management. For sprint zero we can use Dedicated with customer VPC peering + KMS-backed keys for model logs. They flagged SOC2 questions; we should return the completed questionnaire by EOW. I’ll take point and loop in compliance.

lea (AE): Thanks. Need a simple cost estimate for the POC (infra hours + token cost). Can you give a ballpark hourly and a 4‑week rough total? Chao said budget target around $25k for POC but flexible if justified.

mike (solutions): Ballpark: A100 cost proxy = $3.50–6.00/hr (varies by commit/region). Using $5/hr: baseline 1x for 8h/day dev work, plus load tests 6h during week3 with 2 nodes, plus 24/7 for 3 days of run to reproduce live load. Rough infra: (1 node * 8h * 20 dev days) + (2 nodes * 6h) + (2 nodes * 72h) = (160 node-hrs) + (12) + (144) = 316 node-hrs * $5 = ~$1.6k. Token generation cost: assume 1500 offline evals (avg 1.2k tokens in + 200 tokens generation each) and 50 live sessions. If hosted token rate ~$0.0004 per token (example), token volume ~(1500*(1400)+50*(1400))~ 2.2M tokens -> ~$880. Total POC variable cost ~ $2.5k. Add engineering time / SRE support and security (est’d $12–18k). So total ~ $15k–$22k. Within their $25k ask.

chao (customer): That looks reasonable. Two asks: 1) can you guarantee we won’t hit rate limits during burst tests? 2) can we get a short runbook for failover if a node OOMs?

sanjay (infra): We can provision autoscale and temporary burst capacity for the scheduled tests — won't be rate-limited if we pre-allocate. I’ll draft a small runbook with steps: check node logs, fallback to smaller-model variant, restart worker, escalate to oncall. Will include exact command snippets and where to find KV cache metrics.

mike (solutions): I'll prepare a one-page POC runbook + sizing appendix and a short cost breakdown slide. Also preparing the minimal eval set runner (script + seed prompts).

ella (security): I’ll send the SOC2 checklist answers and details on KMS/keys. Note: we need chao’s SOC point of contact to sign an NDA for pulling sample logs into our console.

lea (AE): Great. Action items: mike — sizing + runbook draft by Thu COB; sanjay — autoscale + failover runbook by Thu; ella — SOC2 answers + KMS details by Fri; chao — SOC POC contact + confirm budget by Fri. I’ll set kickoff calendar invite. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled infra window created for load test on 2026-02-18 18:00 UTC (2 nodes).
summary: POC scoping thread for FinServX: token/profile details, suggested A100 sizing (1x baseline + scale to 2x for bursts), rough infra + token cost (~$2.5k infra/token, ~$15–22k total including engineering), success criteria, SOC2/KMS notes, and action items
